title: Settlement finality applies to the payment, not to its correctness, which can be trued up later
content:
A.2.4.1.2.1.2 makes Core GovOps the arbiter — it "makes the final decision in resolving any Disputed Amounts" — but immediately offers an alternative to deciding: "Where amounts settled are subsequently determined to be incorrect, they are trued up in a subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle." A.2.4.1.2.1.2.4 gives Core GovOps the explicit choice: resolve the dispute now, "or... elect to determine the correct amount and true up any differences in a subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle."

This separates two things that ordinarily travel together. The payment is final in the sense that it executes and cannot be clawed back — A.2.4.1.2.1.3 sends Final Amounts into the next Executive Vote. The *number* is provisional, and an error becomes a claim settled against a future cycle rather than a reason to hold up this one.

The benefit is that no dispute can block settlement for the whole ecosystem. A single contested line between one Prime and one Executor would otherwise delay a monthly cycle on which unrelated parties depend.

The cost is that a Prime may be paid the wrong amount and carry the difference as an exposure to a future correction, with no interest mechanism specified. Practically, disagreement becomes a receivable.

The control that keeps this honest is documentation: A.2.4.1.2.1.4 requires Core GovOps to publish a "Correction Calculation" specifying "the errors, the correct amounts, and the adjustments needed" on the Sky Forum under the same tag. Corrections live in the same public thread as the original figures, so a true-up is traceable rather than a quiet netting in a later month.
description: Core GovOps decides disputes conclusively, but may instead pay a provisional amount and correct it in a later cycle via a published Correction Calculation, keeping cash moving despite unresolved
